repo.description:
### Summary

`sshKey.all` and `sshKey.one` return the `privateKey` column verbatim to any caller holding `sshKeys:read`.

PR #4857 (merged 2026-07-20, shipped v0.29.13) established that returning SSH private key material to a caller who merely has read access on a resource is a vulnerability, and added `redactServerSshKey` for it. That helper is applied in exactly two places, both in the `server` router. The `sshKey` router - where the keys actually live - was never touched, so the same disclosure is still reachable one endpoint over.

Verified against `canary` as of 2026-08-07 and confirmed byte-identical in the v0.29.14 release. Also reproduced live against a self-hosted v0.29.1 instance.

### Details

`apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/ssh-key.ts:84-89` - no `columns` projection, so every column including `privateKey` is returned for every key in the organization:

```ts
all: withPermission("sshKeys", "read").query(async ({ ctx }) => {
	return await db.query.sshKeys.findMany({
		where: eq(sshKeys.organizationId, ctx.session.activeOrganizationId),
		orderBy: desc(sshKeys.createdAt),
	});
}),
```

`ssh-key.ts:71-83` - `one` returns the record raw. The organization check is present; redaction is not. `findSSHKeyById` (`packages/server/src/services/ssh-key.ts:56-69`) is a bare `findFirst` with no projection:

```ts
one: withPermission("sshKeys", "read")
	.input(apiFindOneSshKey)
	.query(async ({ input, ctx }) => {
		const sshKey = await findSSHKeyById(input.sshKeyId);
		if (sshKey.organizationId !== ctx.session.activeOrganizationId) {
			throw new TRPCError({ code: "UNAUTHORIZED", ... });
		}
		return sshKey;
	}),
```

`allForApps` (`ssh-key.ts:90-99`) already does the right thing, so the safe pattern exists in the same file:

```ts
allForApps: protectedProcedure.query(async ({ ctx }) => {
	return await db.query.sshKeys.findMany({
		columns: { sshKeyId: true, name: true },
		where: eq(sshKeys.organizationId, ctx.session.activeOrganizationId),
		orderBy: desc(sshKeys.createdAt),
	});
}),
```

Worth noting the asymmetry runs backwards from what an access-control review would expect: the **projected** endpoint is a plain `protectedProcedure`, while the two **unprojected** ones are the permission-gated ones. The gate is on the endpoints that leak.

`redactServerSshKey` is defined at `packages/server/src/services/server.ts:63-75` and has exactly two call sites repo-wide - `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/server.ts:109` (`server.one`) and `:447` (`server.remove`). There are zero occurrences in `ssh-key.ts`.

### Impact

Two things make this materially worse than the `server.one` case that #4857 fixed.

**1. An API key is a full user session, not a scoped token.** The better-auth `apiKey()` plugin is configured at `packages/server/src/lib/auth.ts:418-422` with `enableMetadata` and `references` only - no `permissions` block. The `x-api-key` path resolves the key straight to its user and org membership (`auth.ts:489-566`). So a single `GET /api/sshKey.all` with one API key returns every SSH private key in the organization in one response. For most self-hosters those keys are root on the deploy hosts, which makes one leaked API key equivalent to root on the whole fleet.

**2. The documentation states the opposite.** https://docs.dokploy.com/docs/core/ssh-keys says, verbatim:

> Once you create a SSH Key you will not be able to read the Private Key anymore.

That is true of the UI and false at the API layer, and the page draws no UI/API distinction. A self-hoster reading that page would reasonably conclude the key is write-only after creation, and would treat an API key as less dangerous than it is.

### Suggested fix

Either works; the first is smaller.

- Add a `columns` projection to `sshKey.all`, and to `sshKey.one`'s use of `findSSHKeyById`, mirroring `allForApps`. Any caller that genuinely needs the private key (the deploy path) should read it through a service function rather than through a permission-gated read endpoint.
- Or reuse the `redactServerSshKey` approach - an equivalent `redactSshKey` blanking `privateKey` - for consistency with #4857.

Worth auditing the same pattern anywhere else a row containing `privateKey` is returned from a `.all` / `.one` procedure.

The docs page should also be corrected, or the API brought in line with what it promises.

### Related, for grouping

- **PR #4857** (merged, v0.29.13) - the same class, fixed for `server.one` / `server.remove`. This report is the half it did not reach. It also appears to have shipped without a paired advisory.
- **Issue #4600** (open) - SSH deploy key and TLS private key interpolated into shell commands and logged unredacted (CWE-532).
- **PR #4630** (open) - SSH private key leaking into build-failure notifications.
- Precedent that this class is treated as advisory-worthy: GHSA-wx75-vxph-2m2f and GHSA-hg9j-j5mc-phf5 (Git provider credentials via `.one` endpoints), GHSA-fcq8-wv2q-f758 (user info via `user.one`).

### Reporter notes

Found while auditing the blast radius of an API key on a self-hosted instance. No Dokploy-operated infrastructure was accessed; everything above is from the public source tree plus one instance we operate. Happy to test a patch.
repo.summary: SSH private keys disclosed in full by sshKey.all and sshKey.one - the redactServerSshKey fix from #4857 never reached the sshKey router
